text:
elena: Putting up a quick proposal for an embedded interactive terminal in the first-run experience. Idea: let users run 1-2 SDK commands inline (install + quick auth + sample request) so they can see LLM responses without leaving the console. Mock attached: https://img.redwood.in/embedded-terminal-mock.png tom: Nice. Big question: sandboxing and security. We can't run arbitrary code server-side. This should be a client-side JS sandbox that only hits our hosted API via the user's session token. DevSec should confirm rate limits and CORS constraints. hannah: UX notes: make it opt-in per workspace and always show a short plain-language explanation above the terminal: "Run a sample request in your browser (no data uploaded)." Also provide a one-click copy-to-CLI button for users who prefer local work. devsec-bot: Security checklist: 1) terminal must not eval user JS; use a read-only pseudo-terminal that sends commands to a safe interpreter. 2) sanitize outputs. 3) ensure tokens are scoped to a short-lived demo key when available. 4) rate-limit demo endpoint. Created ticket SEC-812. ux-researcher: From research, users like immediate feedback and code they can copy. We should A/B test inline terminal vs static code + run-in-playground. Hypotheses: terminal increases activation but could confuse non-technical users. Variants: `embedded_terminal|static_snippet`. tom: Accessibility: terminal must expose content via ARIA roles. Screen readers should be able to read output history; implement `role=\"log\"` for output area and `aria-live=\"polite\"` for incremental updates. Ensure keyboard-only users can run commands with Enter and there's a clear focus indicator. hannah: Microcopy: header = "Try a sample request"; preface text = "Run these commands in your browser to see responses. Nothing you type is stored." Primary action below terminal = "Copy to clipboard" and secondary small link = "Open in playground". Add a minimize button that collapses terminal to a single-line CTA. qa: Test plan: coverage for keyboard navigation, screen reader output, line wrapping, and paste behavior. Also unit tests for sanitization and snapshot tests for terminal output. We'll need a fixture for demo responses. devsec-bot: One more: if we offer a demo key, display it masked with a reveal action and `aria-hidden` for the masked section. Avoid pre-populating the user's real token in the demo terminal. elena: Telemetry: events `terminal_shown`, `terminal_command_run` (props: command, success:boolean), `terminal_copied`, `terminal_minimized`, `terminal_dismissed`, `onboard_variant: embedded_terminal|static_snippet`. Include `time_to_first_command` as ms. Add `session_id` and `workspace_id` as props. ux-researcher: Also add a small onboarding survey follow-up for users who used the terminal: `in_app_survey` with question "Did this help you get started?" to measure qualitative lift. tom: Dev snippet for accessibility (devs, adapt as needed): ```
\n

Try a sample request

\n

Run these commands in your browser. Nothing you type is stored.

\n
\n \n \n \n \n \n
\n``` hannah: Also show a short fallback for non-JS environments: a static snippet + link to docs. And add a help tooltip that explains privacy and demo key scope. qa: I'll add end-to-end tests for the feature flag `embedded_terminal_v1` and simulate keyboard + screenreader flows in Cypress+axe. elena: Decision for prototype: build the client-side sandboxed terminal behind `embedded_terminal_v1`, show opt-in banner with short copy, telemetry as Tom listed, ARIA per snippet, devsec to review demo key flow. UX research will run an experiment for 2 weeks comparing activation and satisfaction vs static snippet. Action owners: Tom (impl & a11y), DevSec (demo key & sandbox review), QA (tests), Hannah (copy & research). Thanks :sparkles:
